title: Reinforced Cement Concrete
description: All RCC practice questions, covering Beams, Columns, IS Code Provisions, Methods of RCC Design, Prestress & Footings, Shear/Bond/Torsion, and Slabs as per IS 456:2000 and IS 1343.

questions.text: What is the Limiting Value of neutral axis depth ratio (Xu,max/d) for Fe-415 HYSD Steel Bars?
questions.expl: IS 456 Table gives xu,max/d = 0.53 for Fe250, 0.48 for Fe415 and 0.46 for Fe500.

questions.text: What is the required minimum area of tension reinforcement in beams as per IS 456-2000?
questions.expl: Clause 26.5.1.1 of IS 456 specifies minimum tension reinforcement As/bd = 0.85/fy.

questions.text: In a cantilever beam, main reinforcement is provided:
questions.expl: A cantilever has hogging moment, so tension occurs at the top fibre and main steel is placed above the neutral axis.

questions.text: A simply supported beam is considered as a deep beam if the ratio of effective span to overall depth is less than:
questions.expl: As per IS 456, a simply supported beam is 'deep' when effective span/overall depth < 2.

questions.text: In a singly reinforced beam, the effective depth is measured from its extreme compression edge to
questions.expl: Effective depth is the distance from the compression face to the centroid of the tension reinforcement.

questions.text: The final deflection due to all loads including the effects of temperature, creep and shrinkage, measured from the as-cast level, should not exceed
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 23.2 limits the final deflection under all loads to span/250.

questions.text: The assumption that plane sections normal to the axis before bending remain plane after bending is used
options: In both working stress and limit state methods
questions.expl: The plane-section (Bernoulli) assumption underlies both the working stress and limit state methods of flexural design.

questions.text: Doubly reinforced beam is provided when
questions.expl: Compression steel is added when the depth of the section is architecturally restricted and singly-reinforced capacity is inadequate.

questions.text: In balanced section beam the moment of resistance of concrete is given by
questions.expl: For a balanced section, Mu (concrete) = Q·b·d², where Q is the moment of resistance factor.

questions.text: In over reinforced section area of tensile steel provided is ______ the Area of steel provided in balanced section.
questions.expl: Over-reinforced sections have more tension steel than the balanced amount, so concrete fails first.

questions.text: Minimum percentage of tension steel in an RCC beam for Fe 500 steel is
As per IS 456, the effective length of cantilever shall be taken as
questions.expl: For a cantilever, effective length = clear span + d/2 as per IS 456 Clause 22.2.

questions.text: In a singly reinforced beam, if the permissible stress in concrete reaches earlier than the permissible stress in steel, the beam section is called
questions.expl: Concrete reaching its limit first (before steel) indicates excess tension steel — an over-reinforced section.

questions.text: Side face reinforcement shall be provided in the RC beam when depth of web exceeds
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 26.5.1.3 requires side face reinforcement when the web/overall depth exceeds 750 mm.

questions.text: The maximum percentage of steel in a RCC beam is
questions.expl: IS 456 limits maximum tension (and compression) reinforcement in beams to 4% of the gross cross-sectional area.

questions.text: The maximum shear stress in a rectangular beam is
questions.expl: For a parabolic shear distribution in a rectangular section, max shear stress = 1.5 × average shear stress.

questions.text: The effective depth of R.C.C beam is taken from topmost compressive fiber to the
options: Top of the tensile steel reinforcement
Bottom of the tensile steel reinforcement
Center of gravity of the tensile steel
questions.expl: Effective depth is measured to the centroid (c.g.) of the tension reinforcement.

questions.text: If d and n are the effective depth and depth of the neutral axis of a singly reinforced beam, the lever arm of the beam is
questions.expl: Lever arm = d − (n/3), the distance between the resultant compressive and tensile forces.

questions.text: In a T beam the ratio of span to overall depth should not exceed
questions.expl: For deflection control, the span/overall-depth ratio for a T-beam should not exceed about 20.

questions.text: If the depth of actual neutral axis is more than critical neutral axis, section is
questions.expl: Actual NA depth greater than the critical (balanced) NA depth means excess tension steel — over-reinforced section.

questions.text: The maximum strain in concrete at the outer most fiber is
questions.expl: IS 456 assumes the maximum compressive strain in concrete at the outermost fibre in bending as 0.0035.

questions.text: Overall depth of the beam is obtained by adding effective depth and
questions.expl: Overall depth D = effective depth d + effective cover (cover to centre of bar).

questions.text: The maximum amount of compression reinforcement in doubly reinforced beam is
questions.expl: IS 456 limits compression reinforcement in beams to a maximum of 4% (0.04bD) of the gross area.

questions.text: A doubly reinforced beam is considered less economical compared to a singly reinforced beam because
options: The size of the section is small
The depth of the section is small
Concrete is not stressed to its full value
questions.expl: In doubly reinforced sections, added compression steel means the concrete is not utilised to its full compressive capacity, making it less economical.

questions.text: For a reinforced concrete section, the shape of a shear stress diagram is
options: Rectangular above N.A. and parabolic below N.A.
Parabolic above N.A. and rectangular below N.A.
questions.expl: For a flanged (T) section, shear stress varies parabolically in the flange region above the NA and is roughly uniform in the web below.

questions.text: The maximum reinforcement in RCC slab consists of 10mm bars at 100mm c/c spacing. If it is desired to replace 10mm bars with 12mm bars then spacing of 12mm bars should be
questions.expl: Equal area: spacing = (Area of 12mm/Area of 10mm) × 100 = (113/78.5) × 100 ≈ 144 mm.

questions.text: As per IS: 456-2000 a continuous beam is said to be deep if effective span to overall depth is less than
questions.expl: For a continuous beam, IS 456 defines it as 'deep' when effective span/overall depth < 2.5.

questions.text: A floor slab of thickness t is cast monolithically transverse to a rectangular continuous beam of span L and width B. If L0 is the distance between consecutive points of contraflexure, the effective width of compression flange at a continuous support is
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 23.1.2 gives the effective flange width at a continuous support as bw + 6Df + L0/6.

questions.text: The span to depth ratio limit specified in IS 456:1978 for RC beams ensures that
options: tensile crack width is below a limit
stress in tension reinforcement is less than allowable
deflection of the beam is below a limiting value
questions.expl: Span/depth ratio limits are an indirect (deemed-to-satisfy) method of controlling deflection.

questions.text: The effective width of an RC T-beam flange under compression as per IS 456:2000, with l0 the distance between zero moment points, b the rib width and D the flange thickness, is
questions.expl: IS 456 gives effective flange width bf = l0/6 + bw + 6Df for a T-beam.

questions.text: In the limit state design method, the recommended partial material safety factor (γm) for steel as per IS 456:2000 is
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 36.4.2.1 specifies γm = 1.15 for steel.

questions.text: The partial factor of safety for concrete as per IS 456:2000 is
questions.expl: IS 456 specifies γm = 1.5 for concrete in limit state design.

questions.text: If fck (characteristic strength) is the strength below which not more than 50% of test results are expected to fall, fck in terms of mean strength fm and standard deviation S would be
questions.expl: For a normal distribution the median (50th percentile) equals the mean, so at the 50% level fck = fm (the standard 5% definition instead gives fck = fm − 1.645S).

questions.text: A reinforced concrete structure has to be constructed along a sea coast. The minimum grade of concrete to be used as per IS 456:2000 is
questions.expl: For very severe/coastal exposure conditions, IS 456 requires a minimum grade of M30.

questions.text: The modulus of rupture of concrete in terms of its characteristic cube compressive strength (fck) in MPa as per IS 456:2000 is
questions.expl: IS 456 gives the flexural strength (modulus of rupture) fcr = 0.7√fck.

questions.text: For the given T-beam roof section (span 6.0 m, M20, Fe415), if checked for serviceability limit state of deflection, it will be found that
options: the section is checked for serviceability limit state of deflection
it cannot be judged from the given data
questions.expl: Without the full percentage-of-tension-steel and modification factor data worked out, the deflection adequacy cannot be judged from the given data alone.

questions.text: A reinforced cantilever beam of span 4m, cross-section 150 mm × 500 mm. If checked for lateral stability and deflection, the beam will
options: fail in both lateral stability and deflection
questions.expl: A narrow, deep cantilever (150×500 over 4 m span) is prone to lateral-torsional instability as well as excessive deflection.

questions.text: In a reinforced concrete T-beam (flange in compression), the position of neutral axis will
options: depend on flange thickness relative to total depth and % reinforcement
be at the junction of flange and web
questions.expl: Whether the NA lies in the flange or web depends on the relative flange thickness and the amount of tension reinforcement provided.

questions.text: In case of deep beam or thin webbed RCC members, the first crack that forms is
questions.expl: In deep beams, diagonal tension cracking typically initiates before flexural cracking due to the dominant shear/strut action.

questions.text: Which of the following deformations are important in case of deep beams compared to flexure alone?
questions.expl: In deep beams shear deformation is significant and cannot be neglected as in ordinary flexural beam theory.

questions.text: Shrinkage in a concrete slab
questions.expl: As concrete shrinks and is restrained, tensile stresses develop, leading to tension (shrinkage) cracks.

questions.text: A T-beam roof section has: slab thickness 100mm; rib width 300mm; beam depth 500mm; c/c beam spacing 3.0m; effective span 6.0m; distance between points of contraflexure 3.6m. What is the effective flange width?
questions.expl: bf = l0/6 + bw + 6Df = 3600/6 + 300 + 6(100) = 600+300+600 = 1500 mm (using l0, the distance between contraflexure points, since the beam is continuous), which also satisfies the c/c spacing limit.

questions.text: A T-beam behaves as a rectangular beam of width equal to its flange if its neutral axis
questions.expl: If the NA stays within the flange thickness, the compression zone is entirely flange concrete, so the beam acts as a rectangular beam of flange width.

questions.text: How is the deflection in RC beams controlled as per IS:456?
questions.expl: IS 456 uses the deemed-to-satisfy span-to-effective-depth ratio approach to control deflection.

questions.text: In RCC beams, as the percentage area of tensile steel increases
options: depth of neutral axis does not change
questions.expl: More tension steel requires a larger compression area (and hence a deeper NA) to maintain equilibrium.

questions.text: In the limit state method, balanced design of a reinforced concrete beam gives
options: smallest concrete section and maximum area of reinforcement
largest concrete section and maximum area of reinforcement
smallest concrete section and minimum area of reinforcement
largest concrete section and minimum area of reinforcement
questions.expl: A balanced section utilises both concrete and steel to their permissible limits simultaneously, giving the most economical (smallest) section for the maximum steel that section can take.

questions.text: The maximum percent of moment redistribution allowed in RCC beams is
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 37.1.1 permits moment redistribution up to 30% in continuous beams/frames.

questions.text: A reinforced concrete cantilever porch has thickness t. The main reinforcement steel will be placed
questions.expl: A cantilever porch slab has hogging moment, so tension (and hence main steel) is near the top surface.

questions.text: What is the assumption in the steel beam theory of doubly reinforced beams?
options: Only steel bars will resist tension
Stress in tension steel equals the stress in compression steel
Both concrete and steel will resist compression
questions.expl: In the steel-beam (transformed) theory of doubly-reinforced sections, the tension and compression steel are assumed to be stressed equally.

questions.text: The design ultimate load on the short axially loaded column is computed by which of the following equations?
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 39.3 gives Pu = 0.4fckAc + 0.67fyAsc for short axially loaded columns.

questions.text: What should be the effective length of compression members effectively held in position & restrained against rotation at both ends as per IS code?
questions.expl: For both ends fixed (held in position and restrained against rotation), theoretical effective length is 0.5L; IS 456 recommends a design value of 0.65L.

questions.text: According to IS:456-2000, the maximum reinforcement in a column is:
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 26.5.3.1 permits a maximum longitudinal reinforcement of 6% of gross cross-sectional area (though practically limited to 4% away from laps).

questions.text: A column is regarded as a long column if the ratio of its effective length and lateral dimension exceeds
questions.expl: IS 456 classifies a column as slender (long) if the slenderness ratio (leff/least lateral dimension) exceeds 12.

questions.text: Min. diameter of rod in RCC column as per IS 456 is
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 26.5.3.1(a) requires a minimum longitudinal bar diameter of 12 mm in columns.

questions.text: In an RCC column the minimum number of bars in a square column are
questions.expl: A square (rectangular) column requires a minimum of 4 longitudinal bars, one at each corner.

questions.text: A long column fails in
questions.expl: Slender (long) columns fail primarily by lateral buckling rather than pure material crushing.

questions.text: In case of circular column the minimum number of bars recommended by IS: 456
questions.expl: IS 456 requires a minimum of 6 longitudinal bars in a circular column.

questions.text: The load carrying capacity of a column designed by working stress method is 500 kN. The collapse load of the column is
questions.expl: Collapse load ≈ working load × load factor (≈1.5 for columns): 500 × 1.5 = 750 kN.

questions.text: Columns may be made of plain concrete if their unsupported length does not exceed their least lateral dimension by
questions.expl: IS 456 permits plain concrete pedestals/columns when unsupported length does not exceed four times the least lateral dimension.

questions.text: The effective width of a column strip of a flat slab is
options: One-fourth the width of the panel
Half the width of the panel
questions.expl: In flat slab design, the column strip is taken as half the panel width (with the remainder being the middle strip).

questions.text: The minimum cover provided in the column is
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 26.4.1 specifies a minimum clear cover of 40 mm (or bar diameter, whichever is greater) for columns.

questions.text: The pitch of lateral ties in a column should not be more than
questions.expl: Tie spacing is the least of: least lateral column dimension, 16 × longitudinal bar diameter, or 300 mm.

questions.text: If a column of length L is restrained against horizontal & vertical displacement and is free to rotate at both ends, its equivalent length will be
questions.expl: With both ends pinned (translation restrained, rotation free), the effective length equals the actual length, L.

questions.text: All R.C. columns must be designed for a minimum eccentricity of
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 25.4 specifies minimum eccentricity emin = l/500 + D/30 (subject to a minimum of 20 mm).

questions.text: Maximum spacing of longitudinal bars measured along the periphery of the RC column shall not exceed
questions.expl: IS 456 limits the spacing between longitudinal bars along the column periphery to 300 mm.

questions.text: A compression member is termed as column or strut if the ratio of its effective length to the least lateral dimension is more than
questions.expl: A compression member is classified as a column/strut once its effective length exceeds about 3 times its least lateral dimension; shorter members are treated as pedestals.

questions.text: The purpose of lateral ties in short concrete columns is:
options: To avoid buckling of longitudinal bars
To increase the load carrying capacity
questions.expl: Lateral ties primarily restrain the longitudinal bars from buckling outward under compression.

questions.text: Axial load carrying capacity of an RC column (gross concrete area Ac, steel area As, permissible stresses σc, σs, modular ratio m) is given as
questions.expl: In WSM elastic theory, steel is transformed using modular ratio m, giving P = σcAc + (m−1)σcAs, accounting for the concrete area displaced by steel.

questions.text: The lateral ties in a reinforced concrete rectangular column under axial compression are used to
options: avoid the buckling of the longitudinal steel
reduce the axial deformation of the column
questions.expl: Ties primarily prevent lateral buckling of the compression (longitudinal) reinforcement.

questions.text: In a reinforced concrete beam-column, the increase in flexural strength along with the increase in axial strength occurs
options: beyond the elastic limit of the material
when the yielding of the tension reinforcement governs the strength
when crushing of concrete in the compression zone governs the strength
questions.expl: On the ascending (tension-controlled) branch of the interaction curve, both moment and axial capacity increase together while tension steel yielding governs.

questions.text: IS 456:1978 recommends providing certain minimum steel in an RCC beam
options: to avoid rupture of steel in case a flexural failure occurs
to hold the stirrup steel in position
to provide enough ductility to the beam
questions.expl: Minimum steel ensures the section does not fail suddenly/brittlely upon first cracking (avoids sudden rupture).

questions.text: In an axially loaded spirally reinforced short column, the concrete inside the core is subjected to
questions.expl: The spiral confines the core concrete laterally in addition to the applied axial load, producing a triaxial compressive state.

questions.text: Which of the following are the additional moments considered for design of slender compression members in lieu of deflection in x and y directions?
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 39.7.1 gives additional moments Max = Puℓex²/2000D and May = Puℓey²/2000b for slender columns.

questions.text: An axially loaded column is 300 mm × 300 mm, effective length 3 m. What is the minimum eccentricity of the axial load?
questions.expl: emin = l/500 + D/30 = 3000/500 + 300/30 = 6 + 10 = 16 mm, but IS 456 also requires a minimum of 20 mm, so the governing value is 20 mm.

questions.text: The minimum thickness of a reinforced concrete wall should be:
questions.expl: A minimum RC wall thickness of 100 mm is generally recommended for practical and structural adequacy.

questions.text: The minimum head room over a stair must be:
questions.expl: Building byelaws generally require a minimum stair headroom of about 2.1 m (210 cm).

questions.text: Minimum thickness of load bearing RCC wall should be
questions.expl: Load bearing RC walls are typically required to be at least 100 mm thick.

questions.text: Modular ratio 'm' for M25 grade of concrete is
Permissible deviation from specified dimensions of cross-section of columns & beams as per IS Standard is
questions.expl: IS 456 specifies a construction tolerance of +12 mm and −6 mm on beam and column cross-sectional dimensions.

questions.text: Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structure exceeds
questions.expl: IS 456 recommends expansion joints for structures longer than about 45 m.

questions.text: Which of the following load combinations is NOT considered for the limit state of collapse?
questions.expl: Wind load (WL) and earthquake load (EL) are not applied simultaneously in the same load combination, so 1.5DL+1.5WL+1.5EL is not a valid IS 456/875 combination.

questions.text: Various types of load on a building are
questions.expl: A building must be designed for all applicable loads — dead, live, wind, earthquake, etc.

questions.text: Retrofitting is
options: To upgrade/earthquake resistance of existing building to make it safer
questions.expl: Retrofitting means strengthening an existing structure, typically to improve its seismic/earthquake resistance.

questions.text: Minimum admissible water-cement ratio for mild environmental exposure should be
questions.expl: IS 456 Table 5 permits a maximum free w/c ratio of 0.55 for mild exposure conditions.

questions.text: A cantilever retaining wall should not be used for heights more than
questions.expl: Cantilever retaining walls are generally economical up to about 6 m; beyond that, counterfort walls are preferred.

questions.text: For the modern box-girder bridges deployed in flyovers nowadays
options: The depth of the box girder in the middle is maximum
The depth of the box girder on the support is maximum
The depth remains same along the length
questions.expl: In continuous box-girder bridges, bending moments (and hence required depth) are greatest at the supports, so girder depth is maximum there.

questions.text: The minimum cement content recommended by IS: 456 for RCC with normal weight 20mm aggregates under moderate exposure, in Kg/m3
questions.expl: IS 456 Table 5 specifies a minimum cement content of 300 kg/m³ for moderate exposure.

questions.text: The concrete having a slump of 6.5 cm is said to be
questions.expl: A slump of about 25-100 mm (here 65 mm) corresponds to a 'plastic' workability classification.

questions.text: Minimum spacing between horizontal parallel reinforcement of different size should not be less than
options: Sum of diameter of thinner and thicker bars
Twice the diameter of thinner bar
questions.expl: IS 456 requires the clear spacing to be not less than the diameter of the larger (thicker) bar.

questions.text: The modular ratio for M15 grade concrete, according to IS:456 is
questions.expl: m = 280/(3σcbc); for M15, σcbc = 5 N/mm², giving m = 280/15 ≈ 18.67 ≈ 19.

questions.text: The minimum clear distance between main reinforcement bars is
options: Equal to the diameter of the reinforcing bar
Equal to the size of the aggregate
5mm more than the maximum size of coarse aggregate
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 26.3.2 requires clear spacing to be the greater of the bar diameter or (aggregate size + 5 mm).

questions.text: Expansion joint in masonry walls are provided in wall lengths more than
questions.expl: Expansion joints in long masonry walls are generally provided at intervals exceeding about 40 m.

questions.text: In any case the bearing of a lintel should not be less than
questions.expl: A minimum bearing length of about 150 mm (15 cm) is generally provided for lintels on supporting walls.

questions.text: For good quality cement the specific surface of cement should not be less than
questions.expl: IS specifications require a minimum Blaine's specific surface (fineness) of about 2250 cm²/g for OPC.

questions.text: The number of seismic zones India has been divided into as per IS 1893-2000
questions.expl: India is currently divided into 4 seismic zones (II, III, IV, and V).

questions.text: Maximum spacing of side face reinforcement of beams with web depth more than 750 mm is
options: Width of web of the beam
questions.expl: IS 456 limits side-face reinforcement spacing to the smaller of 300 mm or the web width.

questions.text: The characteristic strength of concrete is defined as that compressive strength below which NOT more than
questions.expl: By definition, characteristic strength is the value below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall.

questions.text: The horizontal distance between parallel main reinforcement in RC slab shall not be more than
questions.expl: IS 456 limits main bar spacing in slabs to the lesser of 3 times the effective depth or 300 mm.

questions.text: As per IS 456-2000, the organic content of water used for making concrete should NOT be more than
questions.expl: IS 456 limits organic matter in mixing water to a maximum of 200 mg/L.

questions.text: The value of ultimate creep coefficient for concrete:
questions.expl: The creep coefficient decreases as the age of concrete at loading increases (more mature concrete creeps less).

questions.text: A column is a compression member with effective length exceeding three times its least lateral dimension. This is applicable to:
questions.expl: This definition of a column/strut applies generally, regardless of the cross-sectional shape.

questions.text: Minimum cement content required for M35 grade of concrete for very severe exposure condition as per IS 456-2000, kg/m3
questions.expl: IS 456 Table 5 specifies a minimum cement content of 340 kg/m³ for very severe exposure.

questions.text: As per IS: 456-2000, minimum recommended grade of concrete for structural use is
questions.expl: IS 456 recommends a minimum grade of M20 for general reinforced concrete structural work.

questions.text: What is the pH value of potable water, as specified by IS 456:2000?
questions.expl: IS 456 specifies that mixing water should have a pH not less than 6.

questions.text: Partial safety factors for concrete and steel respectively may be taken as:
questions.expl: IS 456 limit state design specifies γm = 1.5 for concrete and 1.15 for steel.

questions.text: The characteristic strength of concrete in the actual structure is taken as:
questions.expl: IS 456 assumes the in-situ (structure) strength of concrete as 0.67fck, reflecting differences between cube tests and actual member strength.

questions.text: The characteristic strength of concrete is defined as that strength below which not more than ___ of the test results are expected to fall.
questions.expl: Standard definition: characteristic strength corresponds to the 5th percentile of test results.

questions.text: The minimum grade of reinforced concrete in sea water as per IS 456:2000 is:
questions.expl: For very severe/coastal (sea water) exposure, IS 456 requires a minimum grade of M30.

questions.text: Characteristic strength of concrete is measured at:
questions.expl: Concrete characteristic (design) strength is standardly measured at 28 days of curing.

questions.text: Ordinary concrete is not used for concrete grade
questions.expl: M400 requires special high-strength concrete technology and is beyond the range of ordinary concrete mixes.

questions.text: Characteristic compression strength of M20 concrete is
questions.expl: The 'M20' grade designation itself denotes a characteristic cube compressive strength of 20 N/mm².

questions.text: Water cement ratio is the ratio of
options: Weight of water to weight of cement
Weight of cement to weight of water
Volume of cement to volume of water
Volume of water to volume of cement
questions.expl: Water-cement ratio is conventionally defined as the ratio of weight of water to weight of cement in the mix.

questions.text: The total no. of grades as specified by IS 456-2000 are
questions.expl: IS 456:2000 specifies 15 standard grades of concrete, from M10 up to M60/M65.

questions.text: Compressive strength of concrete is ___ tensile strength
questions.expl: Concrete is much stronger in compression than in direct tension (tensile strength is typically only about 1/10th of compressive strength).

questions.text: Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) was evolved because plain concrete has
questions.expl: Steel reinforcement is added because plain concrete is weak (low) in tension.

questions.text: The size of cube used to determine characteristic compressive strength of concrete is
questions.expl: The standard test cube specified by IS codes is 150 mm × 150 mm × 150 mm.

questions.text: A slump cone is used primarily to provide an indication of which of the following in concrete
questions.expl: The slump test is a simple field indicator primarily of the workability (consistency) of fresh concrete.

questions.text: For the construction of RCC slabs, columns, beams etc the minimum recommended grade of concrete mix is
questions.expl: IS 456 recommends M20 as the minimum grade for reinforced concrete structural members.

questions.text: The modulus of elasticity of M-25 grade concrete (in N/mm2) as per IS: 456-2000 is assumed as
Plain cement concrete has very high
questions.expl: Plain (unreinforced) concrete is characteristically strong in compression.

questions.text: Permissible compressive strength of M200 concrete grade is
questions.expl: As per the older kg/cm² grade nomenclature, M200 corresponds to a permissible compressive strength of about 200 kg/cm².

questions.text: For testing compressive and tensile strength of cement, cement mortar is made by mixing cement and standard sand in the proportion of
questions.expl: Standard cement mortar test cubes/briquettes use a 1:3 cement-to-sand ratio by weight.

questions.text: The ratio between the ultimate tensile stress and the working stress is known as
questions.expl: This ratio, by definition, is the factor of safety used in working stress design.

questions.text: The ratio of collapse load to the working load is known as
questions.expl: This ratio is termed the load factor, linking working stress and limit state (ultimate) concepts.

questions.text: The BIS code which is meant for concrete mix is
questions.expl: IS 456 is the principal Indian code covering plain and reinforced concrete, including mix design provisions (historically referenced as IS 456:1978).

questions.text: The bulk density of ordinary concrete is about
questions.expl: The typical unit weight of ordinary reinforced concrete is about 24-25 kN/m³, which does not exactly match the other given options.

questions.text: The working stress of a material is expected to be
questions.expl: Working (permissible) stress is deliberately kept below the yield stress to provide a margin of safety.

questions.text: To estimate 28-day crushing strength of concrete cubes from 7-day cube strength, we multiply the 7-day cube strength by
questions.expl: As a rule of thumb, 7-day strength is roughly two-thirds of the 28-day strength, so 28-day strength ≈ 1.5 × 7-day strength.

questions.text: The thermal expansion coefficient (α) of steel is
options: 13×10⁻⁶/°C and closely resembles α of concrete
11×10⁻⁶/°C and differs widely from α of concrete
12×10⁻⁶/°C and close to α of concrete
10×10⁻⁶/°C but nearly equal to α of concrete
questions.expl: Steel's thermal expansion coefficient (~12×10⁻⁶/°C) is close to that of concrete, which is why RCC works well as a composite material under temperature change.

questions.text: The concrete mix design is conducted as per
questions.expl: IS 10262 is the Indian standard specifically dealing with concrete mix design/proportioning guidelines.

questions.text: To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of specimen used is
questions.expl: IS 516 specifies a standard flexure test beam of 150 mm × 150 mm × 700 mm for normal aggregate sizes.

questions.text: Approximate value of shrinkage strain in concrete, is
questions.expl: IS 456 assumes an approximate total shrinkage strain of 0.0003 for design purposes (in the absence of test data).

questions.text: The relation between modulus of rupture fcr and direct tensile strength fct is given by
questions.expl: Modulus of rupture (flexural) > splitting tensile strength > direct (axial) tensile strength, as different failure mechanisms give progressively lower apparent strengths.

questions.text: The approximate value of the ratio between direct tensile strength and flexural strength is
questions.expl: Direct tensile strength is typically about half the flexural strength (modulus of rupture) of concrete.

questions.text: The relation between modulus of rupture fcr and characteristic strength of concrete fck is given by
questions.expl: IS 456 gives the modulus of rupture as fcr = 0.7√fck (MPa).

questions.text: According to IS:456-1978, the modulus of elasticity of concrete Ec (in N/mm2) can be taken as
questions.expl: IS 456 provides the empirical relation Ec = 5000√fck (N/mm²) for short-term static modulus of elasticity.

questions.text: The critical section for two-way shear of footing is at the
options: Distance d from the column face
Distance d/2 from the column face
questions.expl: IS 456 defines the punching (two-way) shear critical perimeter at d/2 from the column face.

questions.text: As per IS:456-2000 recommendations, the thickness of footing edge on soils should not be less than
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 34.1.2 requires a minimum footing edge thickness of 150 mm on soil.

questions.text: For a number of columns constructed in a row, the type of foundation provided is
questions.expl: A row of closely-spaced columns is typically supported on a continuous strip footing.

questions.text: Normally counterforts in a retaining wall are spaced at an interval of:
questions.expl: Counterforts in a counterfort retaining wall are generally spaced about 2 to 3 m apart.

questions.text: Most commonly used method of pre-stressing in industries is
questions.expl: The Freyssinet system is one of the most widely used post-tensioning methods in industrial practice.

questions.text: The critical section for two way shear in an isolated spread footing is at the
questions.expl: As per IS 456, punching shear is checked at a perimeter d/2 away from the column/pedestal face.

questions.text: Critical section for calculating bending moment for a spread concrete footing of effective depth d is given by the plane at
questions.expl: IS 456 takes the critical section for maximum bending moment in an isolated footing at the face of the column/pedestal.

questions.text: In reinforced and plain concrete footing resting on soils, the thickness at edge shall not be less than
questions.expl: IS 456 requires a minimum footing edge thickness of 150 mm (15 cm) on soil.

questions.text: Counterfort retaining wall is generally constructed when height of the earth to be retained exceeds
questions.expl: Beyond about 6 m of retained height, counterfort walls become more economical than plain cantilever walls.

questions.text: The loss of prestress due to elastic shortening of concrete is least in
options: multiple wire pre-tensioned beam with sequential cutting of wires
multiple wire post-tensioned beam subjected to sequential prestressing
questions.expl: In a single-wire post-tensioned beam, there is no other tendon whose subsequent stressing would cause additional elastic shortening loss, so the loss is minimal.

questions.text: IS:1343:1980 limits the minimum characteristic strength of pre-stressed concrete for post tensioned work and pretension work as
questions.expl: IS 1343 specifies minimum grades of M30 for post-tensioned and M40 for pre-tensioned prestressed concrete work.

questions.text: In a reinforced concrete retaining wall, a shear key is provided if the
options: shear stress in the vertical stem is excessive
shear force in the toe slab is more than in the heel slab
retaining wall is not safe against sliding
retaining wall is not safe against overturning
questions.expl: A shear key beneath the base slab increases passive resistance, provided when the wall is inadequate against sliding.

questions.text: A buttress in a wall is intended to provide
options: lateral support to roof slab only
lateral support to roof beams only
questions.expl: A buttress is a projecting support built to resist lateral forces on a wall, providing it lateral stability.

questions.text: In a combined footing for two columns carrying unequal loads, the maximum hogging moment occurs at
options: inside face of the heavier column
a section equidistant from both columns
a section having maximum shear force
a section having zero shear force
questions.expl: As in any beam, the bending moment is maximum (here, maximum hogging) where the shear force diagram crosses zero.

questions.text: The critical section for maximum bending moment in the footing under a masonry wall is located at
options: mid-way between the face and the middle of the wall
a distance equal to the effective depth of footing from the face of the wall
questions.expl: For footings under masonry walls, IS 456 takes the critical BM section midway between the wall face and the centreline of the wall.

questions.text: In case of pre-tensioned RC beams
options: Shrinkage of concrete is of the order of 3×10⁻⁴
relaxation of steel can be ignored
only one wire can be stretched at a time
even mild steel can be used for prestressing
questions.expl: The design shrinkage strain assumed for pretensioned members is on the order of 3×10⁻⁴ (0.0003), causing prestress loss.

questions.text: Prestressed concrete is more desirable in case of
options: cylindrical pipe subjected to internal fluid pressure
cylindrical pipe subjected to external fluid pressure
cylindrical pipe subjected to equal internal and external pressures
cylindrical pipe subjected to end pressures
questions.expl: Circumferential prestressing counteracts the tensile hoop stresses caused by internal pressure in pipes, making PSC very suitable for this case.

questions.text: In a load-balanced prestressed concrete beam under self load, the cross-section is subjected to
questions.expl: In the load-balancing concept, the tendon profile is chosen so that the transverse component of prestress exactly balances the self-weight, leaving only a uniform axial stress.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Web shear cracks start due to high diagonal tension in beams with thin webs and high prestressing force
Shear design for a prestressed concrete beam is based on elastic theory
In the zone where bending moment is dominant and shear is insignificant, cracks occur at 20° to 30°
After diagonal cracking, shear transfer mechanism in PSC is very different from RC
questions.expl: In thin-webbed, highly prestressed beams, web-shear cracking occurs due to high diagonal (principal) tensile stresses even before flexural cracking.

questions.text: The magnitude of loss of prestress due to relaxation of steel is in the range of
questions.expl: Relaxation losses in prestressing steel are typically of the order of 2-8% of the initial prestress.

questions.text: The ultimate strength of the steel used for prestressing is nearly
questions.expl: High-tensile prestressing steel (wires/strands) typically has an ultimate tensile strength around 1500-1900 N/mm².

questions.text: In a post-tensioned prestressed concrete beam, the end block zone is the zone between the end of the beam and the section where
questions.expl: The end (anchorage) block is where transverse (bursting/spalling) stresses dissipate; beyond it, only the longitudinal (uniform) stress distribution remains.

questions.text: The propagation of a shear crack in a prestressed concrete member depends on
options: shape of the cross-section of the beam
questions.expl: In PSC members shear-crack propagation is strongly influenced by the geometry (shape) of the cross-section, which governs the stress distribution.

questions.text: In pre-tensioning scheme, pre-stress load is transferred in
options: either single or multi-stage depending on load magnitude
the same manner as in post-tensioning
questions.expl: In pretensioning, prestress is transferred to concrete instantaneously (single stage) when the tendons are released/cut after concrete hardens.

questions.text: In the conventional prestressing, the diagonal tension in concrete
questions.expl: Prestressing induces a compressive stress field that reduces the net diagonal tension in the concrete.

questions.text: In prestressed concrete, high grade concrete is used for
questions.expl: High-grade (high-strength) concrete exhibits lower creep, which helps minimise long-term prestress loss.

questions.text: In the Limit state design of prestressed concrete structures, the strain distribution is assumed to be
questions.expl: As with RC design, the plane-sections assumption gives a linear strain distribution across the depth in PSC limit state design.

questions.text: High strength steel used in prestressed concrete can take how much maximum strain?
questions.expl: High-tensile prestressing steel typically has an elongation/strain capacity of about 4% at rupture.

questions.text: The use of 'concordant cables' in prestressed continuous beam induces
questions.expl: A concordant tendon profile produces no secondary (parasitic) reactions/moments at the supports of a continuous beam.

questions.text: In case of prestressed concrete members, the bursting stresses develop at
questions.expl: Bursting (transverse tensile) stresses arise near the anchorage zone due to the spreading of the concentrated prestressing force.

questions.text: A prestressed concrete section is said to have failed in strength at the moment when all the material in the section has exhausted its
options: Stress as well as strain limitations
questions.expl: In limit state/ultimate design, failure is defined by the material reaching its ultimate strain capacity.

questions.text: Spalling stresses are produced in post-tensioned prestressed concrete members because of
questions.expl: Spalling stresses arise from the highly concentrated anchorage force spreading out over the section near the end of the member.

questions.text: A concordant cable profile in pre-stressed concrete is
options: one which coincides with the centroidal axis of the beam
one which does not cause secondary stresses
questions.expl: A concordant cable profile follows the pressure line of the applied loads such that it produces no secondary (parasitic) stresses in a continuous member.

questions.text: Spalling stresses are produced in post-tensioned prestressed concrete members at
options: locations of maximum bending moment only
questions.expl: Spalling stresses, like bursting stresses, are localized at the anchorage (end-block) zone of post-tensioned members.

questions.text: Shear reinforcement is provided in the form of:
options: Combination of vertical and inclined bars
questions.expl: IS 456 permits shear reinforcement as vertical stirrups, inclined (bent-up) bars, or a combination of both.

questions.text: Tension bars in a cantilever beam must be enclosed in the support up to:
questions.expl: Tension reinforcement must extend into the support by the full development length, Ld, to be adequately anchored.

questions.text: The propagation of a shear crack in a prestressed concrete member depends on
options: Shape of the Cross-section of beam
questions.expl: Shear crack propagation depth in PSC members is affected by the amount and disposition of tensile reinforcement resisting the crack opening.

questions.text: The shear reinforcement has to be designed when nominal shear stress is ___ permissible shear stress
questions.expl: Shear reinforcement is required whenever the applied nominal shear stress (τv) exceeds the concrete's permissible shear strength (τc).

questions.text: In the absence of shear stirrups, where do cracks in an RCC beam constructed in a frame come first?
questions.expl: Shear force is maximum near the supports, so diagonal shear cracks initiate there first in the absence of stirrups.

questions.text: As per IS:456-2000, the shear strength variation along the section is assumed
questions.expl: IS 456 assumes a parabolic distribution of shear stress across the depth of an RC section, similar to elastic beam theory.

questions.text: The minimum spacing of the vertical stirrups to resist shear in a beam, in terms of effective depth 'd', is restricted to
questions.expl: IS 456 limits the maximum spacing of vertical shear stirrups to 0.75d.

questions.text: The development length in tension in HYSD bars when used with M20 grade of concrete is
options: 68 times the nominal dia. of bar
51 times the nominal dia. of bar
46 times the nominal dia. of bar
78 times the nominal dia. of bar
questions.expl: For Fe415 HYSD bars in M20 concrete, IS 456 gives a development length of about 47 (≈46) times the bar diameter.

questions.text: The anchorage value of a 45° bend in reinforcing bar embedded in concrete is assumed to be
questions.expl: IS 456 assigns an anchorage value of 4 times the bar diameter for each 45° bend.

questions.text: Shear reinforcement is provided to resist
questions.expl: Shear reinforcement (stirrups/bent-up bars) is designed to resist diagonal tension cracking caused by combined shear and flexure.

questions.text: For deformed bars, bond stress is
questions.expl: Deformed (ribbed/HYSD) bars mechanically interlock with concrete, giving higher bond stress than smooth, plain bars.

questions.text: The spacing of nominal shear reinforcement is given by
questions.expl: IS 456 gives the minimum shear reinforcement spacing formula Sv = 0.87fyAsv/(0.4b).

questions.text: When the shear stress exceeds the permissible limit in a slab, then to bring the shear stress within limits
options: Steel should be provided on compression side
questions.expl: Slabs generally do not use shear reinforcement, so the depth is increased to reduce the shear stress within permissible limits.

questions.text: When HYSD bars are used in place of mild steel bars, the bond strength
questions.expl: Deformed HYSD bars provide better mechanical interlock, increasing bond strength compared to plain mild steel bars.

questions.text: In limit state method of design, for HYSD bars the values of bond stress shall be
questions.expl: IS 456 permits the design bond stress for deformed bars to be increased by 60% over that for plain bars.

questions.text: The main reason for providing a number of reinforcing bars at a support in a simply supported beam is to resist in that zone
questions.expl: Continuing bars into supports provides sufficient bond/anchorage length to develop the required bond stress there.

questions.text: Torsion resisting capacity of a given RC section
options: decreases with decrease in stirrup spacing
decreases with increase in longitudinal bars
does not depend upon stirrup and longitudinal steels
increases with the increase in stirrup and longitudinal steels
questions.expl: Both closed stirrups and longitudinal steel contribute to torsional resistance, so increasing either enhances torsional capacity.

questions.text: If the nominal shear stress (τv) at a section does not exceed the permissible shear stress (τc)
options: minimum shear reinforcement is still provided
shear reinforcement is provided to resist the nominal shear stress
shear reinforcement is provided for the difference of the two
questions.expl: Even when τv < τc, IS 456 requires minimum (nominal) shear reinforcement to be provided as a precaution against unforeseen forces.

questions.text: In limit state design, permissible bond stress in the case of deformed bars is more than that in plain bars by
questions.expl: IS 456 permits a 60% increase in design bond stress for deformed (HYSD) bars over plain bars.

questions.text: Shear span is defined as the zone where
questions.expl: Shear span refers to the region between a support/load point where the shear force remains constant.

questions.text: Assertion (A): The development length for HYSD Fe 415 bars is less than that for mild steel plain bars. Reason (R): The permissible bond stress for HYSD Fe 415 bars is more than that for mild steel plain bars.
options: both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.expl: Higher bond stress for HYSD bars directly reduces the required development length, so R correctly explains A.

questions.text: Diagonal tension reinforcement is provided in a beam as
options: 90° bend at the ends of main bars
questions.expl: Bent-up (inclined) bars are commonly used, in addition to vertical stirrups, to resist diagonal tension from shear.

questions.text: When HYSD bars are used in place of mild steel bars in a beam, the bond strength
questions.expl: The ribbed surface of HYSD bars improves mechanical interlock, increasing bond strength.

questions.text: What is the bond stress acting parallel to the reinforcement on the interface between bar and concrete?
questions.expl: Bond stress is essentially a shear stress acting along the bar-concrete interface, transferring force between the two materials.

questions.text: The appropriate expression in assessing development length is
questions.expl: Development length is derived by equating bar force (φ²σs/4) to bond resistance (πφLdτbd), giving Ld = φσs/(4τbd).

questions.text: Lap length of reinforcement in compression shall not be less than
questions.expl: IS 456 specifies a minimum compression lap length of 24 times the bar diameter.

questions.text: In a reinforced concrete member, the best way to ensure adequate bond is
options: to provide minimum number of large diameter bars
to provide large number of smaller diameter bars
to increase the cover for reinforcement
questions.expl: Smaller diameter bars in greater number give more total surface area for a given steel area, improving bond.

questions.text: In case of simply supported slabs with free edges, what are the design moments as per code?
questions.expl: IS 456 Annex D gives moment coefficients based on the shorter span Lx for both Mx and My: Mx = axwLx², My = aywLx².

questions.text: What recommendation is given for basic value of span/effective depth ratio in IS code 456-2000 for continuous beams up to 10m span?
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 23.2.1 gives a basic span/depth ratio of 26 for continuous spans.

questions.text: The minimum cover of a slab should neither be less than the diameter of bar nor less than
questions.expl: IS 456 requires a minimum clear cover of 15 mm (or the bar diameter, whichever is greater) for slabs.

questions.text: The minimum reinforcement in slabs should not be less than ___ % of the total cross-sectional area when HYSD bars are used in either direction.
questions.expl: IS 456 Clause 26.5.2.1 specifies a minimum reinforcement of 0.12% of the gross area for HYSD bars in slabs.

questions.text: The ratio of the diameter of reinforcing bars and the slab thickness is
questions.expl: IS 456 limits the maximum bar diameter to 1/8 of the total slab thickness.

questions.text: Distribution steel is provided
questions.expl: In a one-way slab, distribution (secondary) reinforcement is provided transverse to the main steel to distribute load and control shrinkage/temperature cracking.

questions.text: In case of slabs using Mild Steel bars, the minimum %age of steel recommended is
questions.expl: IS 456 specifies a minimum reinforcement of 0.15% of gross area for slabs using mild steel bars.

questions.text: In case of simply supported beam of span 15m, the minimum effective depth to satisfy vertical deflection limit should be
questions.expl: Using the basic span/depth ratio of 20 for simply supported beams: d = 15000/20 = 750 mm.

questions.text: In a two way slab, main reinforcement is provided along
options: Length and width of the slab
questions.expl: In a two-way slab, both spans carry significant moment, so main reinforcement runs in both directions (length and width).

questions.text: The effective span of a simply supported slab is
options: Distance between the centres of the bearings
Clear distance between inner faces of walls plus twice the thickness of wall
Clear span plus effective depth of the slab
questions.expl: IS 456 defines effective span using several criteria (least of distance between bearing centres, clear span + effective depth, etc.), so effectively all apply as governing conditions.

questions.text: For a continuous floor slab supported on beams, the ratio of end span length and intermediate span length is
questions.expl: IS 456's simplified moment coefficient method for continuous slabs applies when the end span is not less than 0.9 times the intermediate span.

questions.text: For cantilever slab, span to depth ratio as per control of deflection is
questions.expl: IS 456 gives a basic span/effective-depth ratio of 7 for cantilever members.

questions.text: If ly/lx > 2.0 the slab is
questions.expl: When the long-to-short span ratio exceeds 2, load transfer predominantly occurs along the shorter span, and the slab is designed as one-way.

questions.text: In a two way slab, main reinforcement is provided along
options: Length and width of the slab
questions.expl: As with Q9, a two-way slab requires main reinforcement in both the length and width directions.

questions.text: A flat slab is supported on
questions.expl: A flat slab is a slab system supported directly on columns without beams.

questions.text: In case of two-way slab, the depth of slab is based on
options: Mostly long span but sometimes short span
questions.expl: Two-way slab depth is generally governed by the shorter span, since it carries a greater share of the load.

questions.text: Minimum percentage of torsion (torsion/corner) steel in RCC slab is
questions.expl: The minimum reinforcement provision of 0.12%bD (as for HYSD main/distribution steel) also applies to torsion steel at corners of two-way slabs.

questions.text: Maximum permitted spacing of main bars in a slab is
questions.expl: IS 456 limits main reinforcement spacing in slabs to the lesser of 3 times the effective depth (3d) or 300 mm.

questions.text: A slab-beam floor system may be supported on brick walls or framed into a system of RC columns. The floor thickness (slab + beam web) for the same span will be
options: less when framed into a system of RC columns
less when supported on brick walls
equal to the wall thickness or size of column
questions.expl: Framing into columns (continuous construction) generally reduces effective span moments/ deflection demand compared to simply-supported wall bearing, allowing a thinner floor system.

questions.text: The sum of nodal forces at any yield line intersection in a slab is
questions.expl: In yield line theory, equilibrium requires that the nodal forces at any yield line intersection sum to zero.

questions.text: Shrinkage in a concrete slab
questions.expl: Restrained shrinkage generates tensile stresses in the slab, leading to tension (shrinkage) cracks.
